means.text: The Nigeria joint development zone. A 2001 treaty set up a bi-national authority over a shared offshore area in the Gulf of Guinea, with petroleum and other resources to be shared. The authority's running costs took 43% of the zone's revenue in 2014 (São Tomé EITI report), so the lever pays for its own administration first.

grand_strategy.reading: São Tomé and Príncipe plays a small hand between Lisbon, which the re-election of Carlos Vila Nova reinforces through language and aid, and Beijing, the recognition it chose in 2016 after dropping Taiwan. Its one large lever is the shared offshore zone with Nigeria, and that lever has so far paid its own authority more than the state. The tests of the coming years are whether the Portuguese summit turns into money and whether the zone ever produces commercial output.

stances.note: Partner with Lisbon, no treaty. Diplomatic relations began 12 July 1975 (Portuguese diplomatic portal, cited on Wikipedia, not opened). Portugal prepared a bilateral summit on education, health, energy and investment with São Tomé in September 2026, and the Portuguese prime minister attended the swearing-in of Carlos Vila Nova on 3 September 2026. Trend warming on that basis. Confidence C: the grade and the bond kin (shared Portuguese language and history) are our reading; the Portuguese government page speaks of cooperation, not of kinship.

stances_toward.note: Rewritten from Nigeria's side on 2026-10-16 (replaces the provisional reciprocal). Partner by treaty-made joint zone: the 2001 Abuja treaty (signed 21 February 2001; the treaty text was not opened, the date comes from the STP card's search results) created the Joint Development Authority over the shared offshore zone, and Nigeria's foreign ministry received an Authority delegation on 27 July 2026 (press release 2026-173, tier 1 for the fact of the meeting). The Guardian (Nigeria, 2018) reads the zone as long stalled. Not an alliance: no defence clause. Bond none, as on the STP card. Same sources as the STP card, so the pair is consistent.
